subject: Hosted API: Proposal to increase committed monthly units and introduce stepped tiers
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Maya Thomas <maya@concourse.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Dec 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted API: Proposal to increase committed monthly units and introduce stepped tiers

Hi Maya —

Thanks for the good conversation yesterday. Based on Concourse's Q1 forecasts and the pattern you shared, we put together a proposed commit uplift that should lower your unit cost while preserving burst capacity for seasonal spikes. High level:

- Move from your current 300M token/month commit to a stepped annual ladder: 350M / 500M / 700M (Q1/Q2/Q3 committed floors) with a blended rate that phases in the discount as you hit each band.
- Maintain existing soft-throttle that allows 10% burst over commit with overage at a nominal rate; introduce a 48-hour auto-burst credit for critical incidents (ops-managed).
- Add a 0.5% SLA buffer credit for latency SLO misses in the first 90 days of the new cadence.

I attached the proposed terms and a short usage forecast so your finance team can model spend. If this looks reasonable I can loop in Billing/SalesOps to prepare a formal amendment and a PO-ready invoice.

Attachments: [proposed-commit-terms-v1.pdf] [usage-forecast-q1-2026.xlsx]

Next steps I recommend:
1) Quick sync this week to confirm tiers and discount bands (30 min) — are you available Thu 10:00am PT?
2) If accepted, we’ll draft a 1-page amendment and a one-time onboarding credit for migration testing.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

---
Redwood Inference — production-first LLM inference (hosted, dedicated, private)
From: Maya Thomas <maya@concourse.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Dec 2025 12:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API: Proposal to increase committed monthly units and introduce stepped tiers

Thanks Rishi — appreciate the draft. A few quick clarifying questions from our side before we book an internal review:

1) How do the blended rates apply if actual consumption drops below the Q1 floor in Q2 (we have a marketing-driven spike in Jan, then a normalization period)?
2) The 48-hour auto-burst credit: is that limited to a number of incidents per quarter or unlimited?
3) On the SLA buffer: can we get a sample calculation for a 95th percentile latency miss (we model response-time penalties into our vendor scorecard)?

Also, can you confirm whether the commit tiers will allow us to pin to a particular model variant (we need predictable latency for an edge deployment)?

If you can answer those and share a one-pager for Finance, we’ll run it by procurement.

—Maya
Maya Thomas
Head of Platform Operations | Concourse.ai
maya@concourse.ai

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Maya Thomas <maya@concourse.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Dec 2025 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API: Proposal to increase committed monthly units and introduce stepped tiers

Maya —

Great questions. Short answers below and I attached a one-page summary for Finance.

1) Blended rates and floor underspend: the blended discount is applied to consumption up to the band. If you fall below the Q1 floor in subsequent quarters, we apply a true-up at quarter-end with a soft reversion mechanism: we’ll credit up to 50% of the net difference back to your next billing period to avoid surprise churn-driven charges. The goal here is to be predictable while encouraging sustained volume.

2) Auto-burst credit: limited to 3 incidents per quarter by default. We can extend at enterprise tier. Each incident grants a 48-hour temporary burst (in addition to the 10% soft-throttle) that does not count toward the committed usage.

3) SLA buffer calc (high level): if 95th percentile latency > SLO, we apply the 0.5% buffer credit per percentage point above SLO, capped at 5% per billing cycle for the first 90 days. I attached a worked example in the one-pager.

Model pinning: yes — you can pin to a Redwood-verified model variant for consistent latency. That will consume committed units normally; we’ll reserve capacity on the dedicated pool for your pinned variant during your spike windows as part of the onboarding checklist.

Attachments: [SLA-exception-buffer.docx] [one-pager-finance-proposal.pdf]

If that looks good, I can draft an amendment with the standard legal redlines and route to Billing for a PO-ready invoice. Also cc’ing Karthik and Steph — can you confirm the discount band approval path (who needs to sign off internally)?

Thanks,
Rishi

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Dec 2025 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API: Proposal to increase committed monthly units and introduce stepped tiers

Rishi —

Reviewed the draft terms and the Finance one-pager. Approve the stepped bands and the 3-incident burst credit for Concourse for Q1 as a standard play (no extra margin erosion). We should hold back one concession: reserve the right to request a 30-day review if utilization stays >120% of committed for two consecutive months. That protects supply without blocking the deal.

I’m fine with the 0.5% SLA buffer for the first 90 days. If they accept, legal can cut a short amendment and Billing will append a PO invoice.

Steph — if you can prepare a quick amendment draft with the two minor guardrails (30-day review clause + incident cap) I’ll greenlight and we can send to Maya.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com
